title: How Much of a Thing Must Remain the Same? Burden-Relative Preservation, Support, Identity, and the Boundary of Reditus
object_of_study: The distinctions that must survive variation for declared preservation, support, history, identity, and return burdens.
main_question: What may change without changing what the active burden requires preserved?
secondary_questions: When can sameness transfer across burdens or support compose across realization levels?
What additional history and cross-regime warrant are needed for continuity or changed identity criteria?

claim_layers.claim: Each exact burden induces the coarsest exact partition sufficient to preserve its output; simultaneous burdens require the intersection of their fiber-equivalence relations.

Cross-burden preservation requires factorization on an admitted domain and justified interface. Substrate support profiles alone do not establish support without an appropriate evidence-bearing witness.
Horizontal burden preservation and vertical support composition are distinct; direct upper support and whole-chain support have separate conditions.
History and provenance are genuine burdens, changed identity criteria require cross-regime warrant, metric tolerance need not be transitive, and endpoint sameness does not establish Reditus.

The bundled finite executable fixture checks 15 constructed properties or counterexamples; those checks are not empirical validation. Two unpublished development manuscripts are superseded for publication reference only, with their histories preserved.

Library classification: diagnostic primary with domain-translation secondary, reflecting the paper's conditional adequacy tests and application interfaces. These retrieval labels are not source-native claims of new authority.

scope: Conditional set-theoretic preservation, simultaneous burdens, cross-burden transport, substrate support profiles and witnesses, vertical composition, provenance, identity, approximate-sameness limits, and the boundary of Reditus.
exclusions: No burden-free identity criterion or automatic identity/continuity from terminal equality.

preserved_meaning: Sameness, support, history, provenance, identity, continuity, and Reditus retain distinct burdens; changed criteria require a warranted bridge.
